title: Ingress telemetry privacy & masking playbook (scratch)
content:
Notes to self / rough playbook for ingress-side telemetry masking and privacy-first sampling

Context and motivation
- We ingest a lot of request-level metadata at edge/gateway. Useful for debugging latency spikes and customer issues, but we must avoid PII leakage and reduce storage/retention liability.
- Objective: a set of pragmatic rules, a small runtime SDK for the ingress adapters, and an ops playbook for audits. Start with minimal, iterate.

Constraints / non-goals
- Non-goal: full cryptographic solutions (HSM, enclaves) at this tranche. We want a pragmatic masking + hashing + token removal pipeline.
- Must not break existing SLO debugging signals (request_id, route, latency histogram) — preserve those.
- Must play nicely with private deployments (enable/disable via config).

High level design ideas (sketchy)
1) Ingress classification pipeline (early in request handling)
   - Stage A: Sensitive field detection (fast heuristics)
     * Rule-based checks (header names, common param names: email, phone, ssn, token, api_key)
     * Simple regexes + token frequency heuristics
     * A lightweight ML model later to detect unstructured PII in free-text parts (defer)
   - Stage B: Mask or transform
     * Header-level masking: configurable allow-list/deny-list for headers retained as-is. Default deny: Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email, Set-Cookie.
     * Body-level heuristics: if content-type is JSON, run field-level mask based on path (e.g., event.user.email -> hash or redact).
     * Query params: mask values for sensitive keys, but preserve param presence for routing analytics.
   - Stage C: Provenance metadata
     * Add telemetry.tagging: masking_version=v0.1, mask_ruleset=baseline, mask_decision=masked|removed|hashed|kept

2) Masking transforms choices (tradeoffs)
   - Redact: replace value with literal '<redacted>' (easy, but loses uniqueness)
   - Hash with salt: deterministic hashing (sha256) with per-tenant salt stored in config — retains ability to group but still risky if salt leaks
   - Tokenize: replace with short stable token (requires token table and lifecycle) — heavier ops burden
   - Pseudonymize for experiments: reversible with KMS-protected key (only for enterprise / private deployments)

Default recommendation (MVP): prefer hashed-with-tenant-salt for identifiers (email, device_id) and redact free-text fields that are longer than N chars or contain whitespace-heavy patterns. Cookies and auth headers: remove entirely.

3) Sampling & retention policies
   - Sampling at ingress: 1) full retention for error cases (status >= 500) for 24 hours; 2) 5% uniform sampling for success traces for 30 days; 3) enriched traces on demand when customer tickets reference request_id (pull archive).
   - Steering: allow per-route overrides. E.g., experimental routes can be 50% sampling.

4) Config surface (runtime flags) — what the SDK must expose
   - masking.enabled: true|false
   - masking.ruleset: baseline|strict|enterprise
   - masking.headers.allowlist: [list]
   - masking.fields.rules: ["event.user.email:hash","event.user.phone:hash","text.*:redact_if_contains_pii"]
   - sampling.policy: {"default": 0.05, "errors": 1.0, "routes": {"/debug/*": 0.5}}  <-- represent as simple encoded string in SDK config for now
   - provenance.tags: true|false
   - tenant_salts.kid: base64 (rotatable)

(Implementation note: keep config flat/simple; avoid deep JSON for first pass)

5) Runtime SDK responsibilities (edge adapter)
   - Provide pre-processing hook: returns sanitized_request + telemetry_meta
   - Be a tiny dependency (<= 150KB compressed) for edge runtimes (node/go/rust)
   - Use streaming masking for large bodies (avoid reading whole request into memory)

6) Logs vs traces vs metrics separation
   - Metrics: counters/histograms, never include PII. Good.
   - Traces/spans: keep span names and timing; avoid including raw request bodies in span attributes.
   - Logs: if logs will store request payloads, ensure masking runs before log emission. Add a log-redaction filter in front of log sink.

7) Backfill & retrofitting strategy for existing data
   - For historical data suspected to have PII: run detection pipeline on archived blobs and mark as candidate for purge. Start with heuristics and escalate to manual review for top-ranked candidates.

8) Audit & QA checklist (ops)
   - Unit tests for every mask rule. Use sample input corpus (tiny) containing edge-case emails, unicode, base64, long blobs.
   - Fuzz tests: random binary/large text -> should not crash parser.
   - E2E: simulate ingress -> pipeline -> long-term storage, then attempt to recover PII (red-team) to validate masking.
   - Ensure masking_version is in metadata for all stored events.

Open questions / tradeoffs (todo)
- Deterministic hashing lets us join events but increases re-identification risk if salt leaked. Are we comfortable with per-tenant salted-hash? Need security review. (Owner: security)
- How to handle attachments/binaries (multipart)? Possibly strip by default and retain only metadata.
- Unstructured text (prompts) may contain PII — do we run an ML PII detector inline? That adds latency. Maybe run asynchronous PII detection and purge if found (we lose realtime grouping).
- UX for customers: provide toggles in Console to increase sampling for troubleshooting. Need guardrails so they can't enable auth-header retention.

Quick sketch: example ruleset (plain text)
- headers.allowlist = ["x-request-id","content-length","user-agent","x-route"]
- headers.denylist = ["authorization","cookie","set-cookie","x-api-key"]
- fields.rules = [
   "user.email:hash",
   "user.phone:hash",
   "user.name:redact_short",
   "prompt:mask_if_contains_email_or_phone"
 ]

Integration notes
- Instrumentation: add a telemetry.trace_tag("masking.version","v0.1") early so that downstream processors can assert compliance.
- Backwards compat: if masking.enabled=false (for private deployments), still emit mask_provenance=disabled to logs so audits note teleport.
- Deploy gates: feature-flag rollout with canary traffic only initially (1% hosts).

Action items (next steps)
- Draft a tiny spec page for eng-observability (Confluence): include example rules, SDK API, and rollout plan. -> PRIYA (this doc as base)
- Quick security sync with Security team to validate hashing vs redact tradeoffs -> schedule by 2025-01-20 -> LIAM
- Prototype a Go middleware (net/http) that implements header allow/deny + simple field path masking for JSON; tests. -> MEI
- Add a small corpus of synthetic events for unit tests (edge cases). -> PRIYA

Quick notes / random thoughts
- Could expose an anonymized ID header (x-anon-id) generated from tenant-salted-hash(user.id) that lets support group events without exposing email. Nice to have.
- For high-volume tenants we might want to do server-side tokenization that maps hashed values to short ids and stores mapping in an LRU cache to maintain low cardinality in metrics. Ops burden though.

Scratchpad examples (pseudo-config lines)
- masking.enabled=true
- masking.ruleset=baseline
- masking.header_allowlist=x-request-id,user-agent,x-route
- masking.field_paths=user.email:hash,user.id:hash,prompt:redact_if_contains_pii

-- end of scratch playbook --

Comments welcome. This is deliberately sketchy; aiming to capture options and concrete next tasks rather than a polished doc.
